summary: Extended the plugin package so the renderer's managed binding, matching Linux native asset, dependency manifest, build manifest, and Skia/font notices ship at the plugin folder root and resolve under the host's plugin load context (ADR-010). src/ArrTags/ArrTags.csproj's PackagePlugin target now derives the managed SkiaSharp.dll from the MSBuild-resolved @(RuntimeCopyLocalItems) and the matching linux-x64 libSkiaSharp.so from @(RuntimeTargetsCopyLocalItems) filtered by the declared PluginRuntimeIdentifier, instead of copying only the main assembly; both are staged next to ArrTags.dll, and the build fails with an Error when either resolved asset is missing. The target also stages $(TargetDir)$(TargetName).deps.json (ArrTags.deps.json), build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, and the licenses/ notices, and deletes any previous archive before zipping so packaging is idempotent. The linux-x64 RID is declared by PluginRuntimeIdentifier and documented as the V1 claim: the measured Jellyfin 12 plugin load context probes only the plugin folder root (not x64/ or runtimes/<rid>/native/), so the native asset must sit next to SkiaSharp.dll, and no arbitrary system Skia library is loaded; multi-RID packaging is not part of V1. build.yaml's artifacts now lists ArrTags.dll, SkiaSharp.dll, libSkiaSharp.so, and ArrTags.deps.json, while name/guid/version/targetAbi/framework are unchanged and assemblies is left empty so Jellyfin's folder scan loads the bundled SkiaSharp.dll. The produced artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip contains, at the root, ArrTags.dll (940,544 bytes), SkiaSharp.dll (489,824 bytes, SHA-256 aaaaa18c68ba1f3a3408b00dff28b11d5705198e17ba9d3aa59222bfd35407c8), libSkiaSharp.so (11,170,296 bytes, SHA-256 66c856eaf1a47a00b23204c30c6ee407987bf5086ecc0a1a6b4fd67526b0cd02), ArrTags.deps.json, build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, and the three licenses/ notices. Validation: tests/ArrTags.Tests/PluginPackagingTests.cs adds five unguarded packaging-contract facts (build manifest artifacts and unchanged identity/ABI, the target's resolved-asset/RID contract, and the shipped notice/license files) plus three package-content facts, guarded on the presence of artifacts/ArrTags_*.zip, that assert the archive holds every build.yaml artifact and the required root files and that the packaged managed/native assets match the pinned hashes with an ELF64 x86-64 header check on libSkiaSharp.so. Live-host validation installed the package on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host; the log records Loaded assembly "SkiaSharp, Version=3.119.0.0, ..." from the plugin folder and Loaded plugin: "ArrTags" "0.1.0.0", startup completed, /proc/<pid>/maps maps ArrTags.dll and SkiaSharp.dll from the plugin folder, and meta.json was written with targetAbi 12.0.0.0 and status Active. Because a full artwork render is not wired until tasks 5.5/5.11, native resolution was confirmed with a byte-for-byte replica of Jellyfin's PluginLoadContext over the exact extracted package with the host's managed and native SkiaSharp preloaded: the plugin ALC bound SkiaSharp to the plugin-folder copy, a native decode/draw/encode call succeeded, and /proc/self/maps mapped the plugin-folder libSkiaSharp.so as a distinct second copy. No ADR, RenderVersion, renderer behavior, or existing passing behavior was changed.

known_limitations: A full artwork render through the live Jellyfin host is not wired until tasks 5.5/5.11, so the live host confirms plugin discovery/load and that the plugin-folder managed SkiaSharp.dll is loaded into the plugin load context, but the host did not invoke the renderer. Native resolution of the packaged root libSkiaSharp.so was therefore demonstrated with a byte-for-byte replica of Jellyfin's PluginLoadContext over the exact extracted package rather than by a host render.

The shipped ArrTags.deps.json is the standard RID-agnostic plugin dependency manifest and still references runtimes/linux-x64/native/libSkiaSharp.so, while the package flattens the native asset to the plugin folder root. This is intentional and harmless because Jellyfin constructs AssemblyDependencyResolver with the plugin folder (which discovers no deps.json) and the effective mechanism is Jellyfin's folder DLL scan plus same-directory native probing; the deps.json is shipped for completeness as the task requires.

build.yaml artifacts lists the shipped runtime files (ArrTags.dll, SkiaSharp.dll, libSkiaSharp.so, ArrTags.deps.json) but not build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, or the licenses/ notices, matching the pre-existing convention in this repository where those additional files are shipped by the custom PackagePlugin target. A repository manifest built with jprm from artifacts alone would list the runtime files; if this project later switches to jprm packaging, the notices and licenses would need to be added to artifacts to preserve the ADR-010 license obligation.
V1 claims only linux-x64. The package carries the single linux-x64 native asset and does not ship or load native assets for other Linux RIDs; multi-RID packaging is not part of V1.

The zip file is not byte-for-byte reproducible because MSBuild's ZipDirectory records source file timestamps, but every shipped asset is pinned and its content is hash-asserted by the package-content tests and the manual inspection.
